report.executive_summary: Qualcomm experienced a high-volatility financial trajectory between fiscal years 2023 and 2025, characterized by a sharp recovery in 2024 followed by a severe profitability contraction in 2025 despite continued revenue growth. The primary driver of the 2025 earnings collapse was a $5.7 billion charge related to the Corporate Alternative Minimum Tax (CAMT), which reduced net income by 45% to $5.5 billion while operating income grew 23%. Concurrently, the company’s disclosure posture shifted from explaining cyclical downturns to managing structural risks, including confirmed revenue loss from Apple’s vertical integration, the addition of Xiaomi as a top-tier customer, and new legal and supply chain complexities. While operating cash flow remained robust and grew 15% in 2025, the divergence between cash generation and net income highlights the significant impact of one-time tax adjustments and litigation settlements on reported earnings quality.
report.longitudinal_analysis: The longitudinal disclosure landscape reveals a transition from operational mitigation to structural risk management. In 2023, disclosures focused on explaining revenue declines through macroeconomic headwinds and inventory drawdowns, alongside a one-time fine reversal benefit. In 2024, the narrative shifted to recovery, with the removal of inventory risk warnings and the introduction of specific AI market forecasts and new customer dependencies (Xiaomi). However, the 2025 filing marked a significant increase in granular risk disclosures, explicitly confirming Apple’s switch to in-house modems and detailing OEM anti-royalty strategies. Conversely, transparency regarding tax mechanics decreased; specific FDII explanations and OECD Pillar Two updates were removed. The legal narrative also evolved, with the specific Transsion litigation details from 2024 being removed in 2025, suggesting a shift from specific enforcement actions to broader contractual expiration risks.
report.financial_analysis: Financial trends indicate strong operational cash generation masking significant net income volatility. Total assets grew from $51.0 billion in 2023 to a peak of $55.2 billion in 2024, then contracted to $50.1 billion in 2025, largely driven by the revaluation of deferred tax assets. Operating income rebounded strongly from $7.8 billion in 2023 to $12.4 billion in 2025, growing at a 23% rate in the most recent year. However, Net Income fell 45% to $5.5 billion in 2025 due to the $5.7 billion CAMT valuation allowance. EPS followed this pattern, dropping from $8.97 in 2024 to $5.01 in 2025. Conversely, operating cash flow improved steadily, rising from $11.3 billion in 2023 to $14.0 billion in 2025. The 'Operating cash flow / net income' ratio surged from 1.20 in 2024 to 2.53 in 2025, indicating that cash conversion remained strong despite the earnings hit. Current ratios remained healthy and increased from 2.33 in 2023 to 2.82 in 2025, reflecting improved liquidity positions despite the asset contraction.
limitations: The 'One Big Beautiful Bill' referenced in tax disclosures is likely a placeholder or erroneous text not corresponding to known US legislation, which may impact the accuracy of tax liability interpretations.

Financial analysis is constrained to the limited set of extracted metrics (Assets, Current Assets, Debt, EPS, Liabilities, Cash Flow, Net Income, Operating Income, Shares). Key drivers such as Revenue by segment, Gross Margin, and specific litigation settlement amounts (other than the implied impact on Net Income) are not available in the structured financial data for calculation.

Several disclosure trends are based on the presence or absence of text rather than quantitative financial performance, limiting the ability to correlate disclosure changes directly with specific financial variances.

key_findings.title: Reversal of Financial Performance and Segment Growth
key_findings.analysis: In the comparison between fiscal years 2023 and 2024, Qualcomm disclosed a significant turnaround in financial results. Fiscal 2024 saw revenues increase by 9% to $39.0 billion and net income rise by 40% to $10.1 billion, reversing the previous year's 19% revenue decrease and 44% net income drop. This recovery was driven by a 9% increase in QCT segment revenues (boosted by handsets and automotive) and a 5% increase in QTL segment revenues. The disclosure explicitly shifted the narrative from declining drivers in 2023 ($7.2B QCT decrease) to growing drivers in 2024 ($2.7B QCT increase).

key_findings.title: Introduction of New Regulatory and Supply Chain Risks
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 filing introduced two new risk disclosures absent in 2023. First, Qualcomm flagged the OECD Pillar Two global minimum tax framework, noting that legislation in certain countries will apply starting in fiscal 2025, though no material impact is currently expected. Second, a new risk factor was added regarding the sourcing of critical integrated circuit products from suppliers in China, highlighting specific geopolitical and operational dependencies beyond just revenue exposure to Chinese OEMs.

key_findings.title: Removal of Past Operational Constraints and Contextual Explanations
key_findings.analysis: Several disclosures present in 2023 were removed in 2024, altering the baseline for interpreting the company's operational history. The explanation for 2023 revenue weakness (macroeconomic headwinds and inventory drawdowns) was omitted. Additionally, the disclosure clarifying that QTI cannot grant licenses for parent-owned patents was removed, potentially obscuring the legal structure of the QTL segment. Finally, the detailed disclosure regarding the Q1 2023 segment restatement (reclassifying RFFE revenues) was removed, indicating the financial structure has stabilized since that change.

key_findings.title: Reversal in Handset Market Demand Outlook
key_findings.analysis: The industry trend disclosure shifted significantly from 2023 to 2024. In 2023, Qualcomm projected a mid-to-high-single-digit decrease in global 3G/4G/5G handset volumes for calendar year 2023. For 2024, the outlook reversed to a low-to-mid-single-digit increase, with specific high single-digit to low double-digit growth expected for 5G handsets. This change reflects a fundamental shift in the expected volume drivers for the company's primary segment.

key_findings.title: Reversal of QCT Revenue Trends Indicates Business Recovery
key_findings.analysis: In the comparison between fiscal years 2023 and 2024, Qualcomm’s QCT segment revenue shifted from a $7.9 billion decrease driven by macroeconomic weakness and inventory drawdowns to a $2.8 billion increase driven by inventory normalization and higher handset chipset shipments. This reversal signals a material improvement in demand drivers and business recovery, contrasting sharply with the prior year's decline.

key_findings.title: Introduction of Material Legal Proceedings Risk
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 filing introduces a new disclosure in the 'Looking Forward' section warning that unfavorable resolutions of various legal proceedings could have a material adverse effect on the business. This explicit forward-looking risk warning was not present in the 2023 text, which focused on other restructuring aspects, marking a new substantive risk factor for investors.

key_findings.title: Shift in Capital Expenditure Strategy Signals Growth Intent
key_findings.analysis: Capital expenditure guidance shifted from a reduction to $1.5 billion in 2023 (due to macroeconomic weakness) to a further reduction to $1.0 billion in 2024, but with a critical forward-looking addition: an expectation of near-term increases to support growth and diversification initiatives. This change in capital allocation strategy indicates a pivot toward future expansion despite current low spending.

key_findings.title: Removal of FDII Tax Rate Impact Disclosure Reduces Transparency
key_findings.analysis: The 2023 filing explicitly disclosed a significant variance in the effective income tax rate (1% vs 13%) attributable to Foreign-Derived Intangible Income (FDII) deductions. The removal of this specific quantification and explanation in the 2024 filing alters the transparency regarding the components of the company's tax expense and the drivers of its effective tax rate compared to the prior year.

key_findings.title: New Risk of Margin Compression from Process Technology Transitions
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure adds a specific risk factor stating that transitions to new leading process technology nodes are expected to drive product cost increases, potentially negatively impacting margins. This expands the prior year's supply chain risk disclosures, which were limited to general capacity constraints and supply disruption risks, by introducing a specific technological cost headwind.

key_findings.title: New IP Litigation and Licensing Dynamics with Key OEMs
key_findings.analysis: A new disclosure in 2024 details specific litigation against Transsion Holdings Limited to enforce IP rights, alongside ongoing negotiations with key OEMs including Huawei. This introduces specific legal and strategic engagement factors into the licensing business landscape that were not explicitly detailed in the 2023 filing, highlighting enforcement actions and negotiation statuses with major clients.

key_findings.title: Removal of One-Time EC Fine Benefit Clarifies Income Composition
key_findings.analysis: The 2023 filing quantified a $1.1 billion one-time benefit from the reversal of a 2018 European Commission fine within other income. The removal of this specific disclosure in the 2024 filing indicates the absence of such a material non-operating gain, changing the view of the company's financial performance drivers from one impacted by significant one-time gains to a different baseline.

key_findings.title: Shift in Investment Portfolio Performance from Losses to Gains
key_findings.analysis: The 2023 disclosure highlighted net losses on marketable securities driven by fair value changes in early-stage investments. Its removal in 2024 coincides with a shift to discussing gains on non-marketable equity investments. This represents a material change in the nature of the financial instrument (marketable vs. non-marketable) and the direction of financial impact (loss vs. gain), altering the risk profile presentation of the investment portfolio.

key_findings.title: Removal of Forward-Looking Inventory Demand Risks
key_findings.analysis: The 2023 filing contained forward-looking statements warning that customer inventory drawdowns and weaker demand could lead to excess or obsolete inventory charges. The removal of this specific operational risk disclosure in 2024 suggests a change in the company's assessment of near-term inventory health and demand uncertainty, potentially indicating stabilized supply-demand dynamics or a strategic shift in communication regarding operational risks.

key_findings.title: Introduction of Customer Vertical Integration Risk
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 filing introduces a new risk factor warning that largest customers are developing their own integrated circuit products or choosing competitors' products, which could significantly reduce revenues. This specific business model threat was not explicitly disclosed in the prior year's risk summary, adding a new dimension to the competitive landscape analysis.

key_findings.title: Significant Decrease in Net Income Despite Revenue Growth (FY2025)
key_findings.analysis: In fiscal 2025, Qualcomm reported revenues of $44.3 billion, a 14% increase from fiscal 2024. However, net income sharply declined by 45% to $5.5 billion, reversing the 40% growth seen in the prior year. This divergence highlights a substantial erosion in profitability margins or the impact of one-time charges during the period.

key_findings.title: $5.7 Billion Tax Charge Due to Corporate Alternative Minimum Tax (CAMT) Implementation
key_findings.analysis: Qualcomm recorded a $5.7 billion charge to establish a valuation allowance against its federal deferred tax assets in Q4 2025. This was triggered by the enactment of the 'One Big Beautiful Bill' (OBBB), which subjects the company to the Corporate Alternative Minimum Tax (CAMT) starting in fiscal 2026. The company now expects to be perpetually subject to CAMT, rendering the realization of deferred tax assets unlikely. This represents a major shift in tax liability and financial position.

key_findings.title: Strategic Acquisition of Alphawave ($2.4 Billion)
key_findings.analysis: Qualcomm announced an agreement to acquire Alphawave for approximately $2.4 billion in cash or stock, with completion expected in Q1 2026. This marks a significant strategic expansion and capital commitment not present in the prior year's disclosures, aimed at broadening the company's product portfolio.

key_findings.title: Addition of Xiaomi as Significant Customer
key_findings.analysis: For fiscal 2024, Xiaomi became a significant customer, with revenues comprising 10% or more of consolidated revenues, joining Apple and Samsung. This expands the revenue concentration risk from two major OEMs to three, altering the customer base composition compared to fiscal 2023.

key_findings.title: Quantitative Forecasts for Generative AI and AI PC Adoption
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosures introduced specific quantitative market data: analysts estimate 46% of smartphones sold in 2027 will be generative AI-capable (up from 19% in 2024), and 50% of PCs sold by 2027 will be AI-capable (up from 22% in 2024). Additionally, the Snapdragon X Series AI PCs were highlighted as a new product launch. These updates provide concrete metrics for edge AI adoption, shifting from the qualitative vision presented in 2023.

key_findings.title: New Risk Factor: Licensing Revenue Dependency on Licensee Success
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 filing introduced a new risk statement noting that the core licensing business depends on licensees' ability to develop and deliver high-volume products with customer acceptance. This dependency is outside Qualcomm's control and represents a distinct operational risk not previously disclosed in the same manner.

key_findings.title: Removal of Near-Term Manufacturing Underutilization Assertion
key_findings.analysis: The 2023 disclosure explicitly stated that the company was 'currently experiencing' and 'expecting to continue to experience' near-term underutilization of manufacturing facilities. The 2024 disclosure removed this forward-looking assertion of persistent low utilization, limiting the risk to potential future declines in utilization rates due to demand decreases or failed designs. This narrows the disclosed operational condition.

key_findings.title: Removal of Transsion Litigation and Licensing Disclosure
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 filing disclosed specific license agreements with Transsion and ongoing litigation against them to enforce IP rights. This specific legal and commercial development was removed from the 2025 'Looking Forward' section. The removal of this litigation status and licensing detail represents a significant change in the company's legal exposure and strategic posture regarding enforcement actions.

key_findings.title: Shift from General Competition to Confirmed Revenue Loss from Apple
key_findings.analysis: In the 2025 filing, Qualcomm moved from a general warning about vertical integration competition in 2024 to explicitly confirming that Apple has already switched to its own modem products and that Samsung is also vertically integrating. The disclosure now states this will have a 'significant negative impact' on QCT revenues and cash flows, transforming a forward-looking risk into a confirmed operational reality.

key_findings.title: Expansion of Supply Chain and Manufacturing Risk Disclosures
key_findings.analysis: The 2025 filing introduces several new, granular supply chain and manufacturing risks not present in 2024. These include specific exposure to systemic disruptions (climate, geopolitical, cyber), cost/pricing misalignments with suppliers, and the financial risk of purchasing equipment based on uncommitted forecasts. These changes highlight a broader and more complex set of operational vulnerabilities.

key_findings.title: Introduction of Material Capital Commitment and New ESG Risks
key_findings.analysis: Qualcomm disclosed a new $2.3 billion cash restriction related to the pending acquisition of Alphawave, a significant capital commitment not previously reported. Additionally, new risks were introduced regarding automotive entry barriers, specifically the liability of customer-mandated ESG targets (e.g., net-zero commitments), where failure to meet these standards could result in lost sales.

key_findings.title: Structural Separation of Licensing Portfolio and Agreement Risks
key_findings.analysis: Qualcomm split a previously combined risk disclosure into three distinct factors: a general summary, a specific risk regarding the necessity of evolving the patent portfolio for 5G/next-gen technologies, and a detailed risk regarding the inability to renew or renegotiate expiring license agreements. This structural change isolates technology obsolescence risks from contractual execution risks.

key_findings.title: Removal of Specific Apple Margin Risks and Financial Segment Details
key_findings.analysis: The 2025 filing removed specific 2024 disclosures that quantified the financial risk of Apple purchasing lower-margin MDM products and taking device share. Additionally, details regarding discontinued operations (Non-Arriver, Active Safety, Restraint Control) and specific restructuring charge trends were removed, potentially obscuring historical operational efficiency and specific customer dependency impacts.

key_findings.title: Consolidation and Specification of OEM Anti-Royalty Strategies
key_findings.analysis: In the transition from 2024 to 2025, Qualcomm consolidated previous fragmented disclosures regarding Standard-Essential Patent (SEP) challenges into a single, detailed statement. The 2025 disclosure explicitly categorizes the strategies employed by Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) to limit royalty collections, including specific litigation types (FRAND violations, patent exhaustion), lobbying for compulsory licensing, collective action, and attempts to shift royalty obligations to suppliers. This expansion provides a more granular view of the threat to Qualcomm's licensing business model compared to the broader, separate mentions in 2024, indicating a heightened focus on these specific adversarial tactics.

key_findings.title: Introduction of AI-Specific Intellectual Property Uncertainty
key_findings.analysis: A new risk factor was introduced in 2025 regarding the intellectual property (IP) ownership and license rights associated with AI technologies. As Qualcomm integrates more AI into its products, the disclosure highlights that U.S. and foreign courts and laws have not fully addressed these rights, creating a risk of losing IP rights or facing infringement claims. This represents a new legal exposure area not present in the 2024 disclosure.

key_findings.title: Shift in QTL Revenue Drivers: From Organic Growth to Litigation Settlements
key_findings.analysis: The primary driver for Qualcomm Technology Licensing (QTL) revenue changed materially between 2024 and 2025. In 2024, QTL revenue growth was attributed to a $266 million increase in licensing revenues, part of a broader increase in equipment and services revenue. In 2025, the $143 million increase in licensing revenue is explicitly attributed to a one-time settlement gain in the second quarter, rather than organic volume growth. This shift indicates a greater reliance on litigation outcomes for licensing revenue generation and may impact the perceived sustainability of earnings quality.

key_findings.title: Fundamental Shift in QTL Revenue Dynamics Due to License Expirations
key_findings.analysis: Qualcomm's QTL segment experienced flat revenues and earnings before tax (EBT) in fiscal 2025, contrasting with the growth seen in 2024. The 2025 disclosure attributes this stagnation to the expiration of major agreements (e.g., with Huawei) and the time required to negotiate new long-term licenses with key Chinese OEMs (such as Transsion) to resolve litigation. This marks a transition from a volume-driven growth model to one constrained by contract expirations and new negotiation cycles, increasing revenue volatility risk.

key_findings.title: Cessation of Adverse R&D Capitalization Tax Impact
key_findings.analysis: The 2025 disclosure introduces a new item confirming that the adverse cash flow impact of the R&D capitalization requirement (part of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, OBBB) is expected to cease beginning in fiscal 2026. The previous year's disclosure detailed the ongoing impact from 2023 through 2025. This change positively impacts the future outlook for Qualcomm's cash flows and tax provision, representing a material improvement in financial dynamics.

key_findings.title: New Disclosure of Tariff and Trade Policy Risks
key_findings.analysis: A new specific disclosure in 2025 details the risk of tariffs and global trade policy changes negatively impacting demand, pricing, and costs, and contributing to excess or obsolete inventory charges. This moves beyond the general mention of geopolitical tensions found in previous years, quantifying a specific operational risk exposure related to trade actions by the U.S., China, and other countries.

key_findings.title: Debt Refinancing Activities in Fiscal 2025
key_findings.analysis: The 2025 disclosure includes specific details of debt refinancing activities, including the repayment of $1.4 billion in maturing notes and the issuance of $1.5 billion in new unsecured fixed-rate notes in May 2025. This is a new disclosure element that changes the capital structure, introduces new interest rate obligations (fixed vs. floating via swaps), and establishes new maturity profiles (2030-2035), information not present in the 2024 filing.

key_findings.title: Removal of Specific Financial Consequences of Legal Challenges
key_findings.analysis: Qualcomm removed a 2024 disclosure that explicitly linked legal challenges to concrete financial consequences, such as potential cuts to R&D, suspension of capital return programs, and impacts on debt repayment ability. The removal of this specific commentary obscures the direct cash flow and strategic investment implications of legal proceedings, reducing transparency regarding the potential severity of legal risks on capital allocation.

key_findings.title: Removal of OECD Pillar Two Tax Implementation Disclosure
key_findings.analysis: The 2025 filing removed the 2024 disclosure regarding the OECD Pillar Two global minimum tax legislation, which was noted to apply beginning in fiscal 2025. While the company previously stated it did not expect a material impact, the complete removal of this update suggests a change in disclosure posture regarding this significant international tax risk, potentially due to resolved uncertainty or a decision to omit it from the main results section.

key_findings.title: Removal of Forward-Looking IP Protection Risk Commentary
key_findings.analysis: Qualcomm removed a 2024 'Looking Forward' statement that specifically cautioned that the continued success of its licensing programs depended on evolving its patent portfolio and that failure to protect IP could lead to misappropriation or loss of enforcement ability. The removal of this explicit strategic risk commentary, while the underlying risk likely remains, changes the transparency of how the company communicates vulnerabilities in its intellectual property protection strategy.

materiality.reason: The disclosure detailed a significant change in accounting policy and segment reporting structure occurring in Q1 2023 (reclassification of RFFE revenues). The removal of this disclosure in the 2024 filing, with no counterpart describing a new or continuing restatement policy, indicates that the 2024 financials are based on a stable, post-change structure. This removal clarifies the baseline for comparability. The absence of the restatement note is material because it confirms the finality of the segment restructure, affecting how users interpret trends in Handsets, Automotive, and IoT streams without the complication of prior-period recasts.
materiality.key_change: Removal of Q1 2023 segment restatement disclosure

sources.text: (1) Beginning in the first quarter of fiscal 2023, QCT RFFE (radio frequency front-end) revenues, which were previously presented as a separate revenue stream, are now included within our Handsets, Automotive and internet of things (IoT) revenue streams as applicable.
Prior period information has been recast to reflect this change.
Descriptions of our three QCT revenue streams can be found in this Annual Report in "Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements, Note 2. Composition of Certain Financial Statement Items."

materiality.reason: The disclosure presents the primary financial results, showing a significant turnaround in financial performance. Revenues increased 9% to $39.0 billion and net income increased 40% to $10.1 billion. This change from a 19% revenue decrease in the prior year to a 9% increase, coupled with substantial profit growth, is a material change in the company's financial position and operational results.
materiality.key_change: Reversal to significant revenue and income growth

sources.text: Revenues were $35.8 billion, a decrease of 19% compared to revenues of $44.2 billion in fiscal 2022, with net income of $7.2 billion, a decrease of 44% compared to net income of $12.9 billion in fiscal 2022.

Revenues were $39.0 billion, an increase of 9% compared to revenues of $35.8 billion in fiscal 2023, with net income of $10.1 billion, an increase of 40% compared to net income of $7.2 billion in fiscal 2023.

materiality.reason: The disclosure reports a fundamental shift in the performance of the largest operating segment (QCT). QCT revenues increased 9% (driven by handsets and automotive) after a 19% decrease in the prior year. This represents a material change in the company's core business dynamics and exposure to consumer/automotive markets.

• QCT revenues increased by 9% in fiscal 2024 compared to the prior year, primarily due to higher handsets and automotive revenues, partially offset by lower IoT revenues.

materiality.reason: The disclosure explained the primary drivers of revenue weakness in fiscal 2023 (macroeconomic headwinds and inventory drawdowns). Its removal means the 2024 filing does not explicitly reference these specific past drivers in the same context. While the macro environment may have improved, the explicit removal of the causal explanation for the prior year's performance changes the narrative baseline for understanding the company's recent operational history and current position relative to those specific headwinds. This is a substantive change in how the company's recent financial performance is contextualized.
materiality.key_change: Removal of fiscal 2023 revenue weakness drivers

sources.text: • Revenues were negatively impacted by the weakness in the macroeconomic environment (which negatively impacted consumer demand for smartphones and other devices that incorporate our products and technologies) and our customers drawing down on their inventory (which were at elevated levels).

materiality.reason: The disclosure reports a significant change in the QTL segment's performance, with revenues increasing 5% after a 17% decrease. The addition of specific drivers ('estimated sales of 3G/4G/5G-based multimode products') quantifies the recovery in the licensing business, which is a critical part of the company's strategic model. This is a material change in financial exposure and segment performance.
materiality.key_change: QTL segment revenue recovery and driver disclosure

sources.text: • QTL revenues decreased by 17% in fiscal 2023 compared to the prior year.
• QTL revenues increased by 5% in fiscal 2024 compared to the prior year, primarily due to an increase in estimated sales of 3G/4G/5G-based multimode products.

materiality.reason: This is a newly introduced disclosure regarding the OECD Pillar Two global minimum tax framework. New regulatory and legislative risks, particularly those with specific implementation dates (fiscal 2025) and potential material financial impacts, are inherently material disclosures for investors assessing future liabilities and tax positions.
materiality.key_change: Introduction of OECD Pillar Two global minimum tax risk and impact assessment

sources.text: The OECD has announced a framework to implement a global minimum tax of 15% (referred to as Pillar Two).
Certain countries have implemented or are in the process of implementing the Pillar Two legislation, which will apply to us beginning in fiscal year 2025.

While we do not currently expect this to materially impact our consolidated financial statements, we continue to monitor the impact as countries implement legislation and the OECD provides additional guidance.

materiality.reason: The 2023 disclosure explicitly defined a critical legal and operational constraint: Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. (QTI) has no authority to grant licenses for patents owned by the parent company. The removal of this disclosure in 2024 represents a loss of clarity regarding the corporate structure governing intellectual property licensing, which is central to the company's QTL segment and overall business model. The absence of a counter-disclosure leaves the relationship between QTI and the parent company's patent portfolio undefined in the provided text, constituting a meaningful change in disclosed operational risk and structure.
materiality.key_change: Removal of QTI patent licensing authority constraint

sources.text: Our reportable segments are operated by QUALCOMM Incorporated and its direct and indirect subsidiaries.
QTL is operated by QUALCOMM Incorporated, which owns the vast majority of our patent portfolio.

Substantially all of our products and services businesses, including QCT, and substantially all of our engineering and research and development functions, are operated by Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. (QTI), a wholly-owned subsidiary of QUALCOMM Incorporated, and QTI's subsidiaries.
Neither QTI nor any of its subsidiaries has any right, power or authority to grant any licenses or other rights under or to any patents owned by QUALCOMM Incorporated.

materiality.reason: The 2024 filing adds a new disclosure point regarding the sourcing of critical integrated circuit products from suppliers in China. While revenue from Chinese OEMs was known, the supply chain dependency on Chinese manufacturers is a new, specific geopolitical and operational risk exposure not detailed in the 2023 filing.
materiality.key_change: Introduction of Chinese IC supplier sourcing risk

We also source certain critical integrated circuit products from suppliers in China.

materiality.reason: The disclosure changes the market outlook from a 'mid-to-high-single-digit decrease' in handset volumes (2023) to a 'low-to-mid-single-digit increase' (2024), with specific high single-digit to low double-digit growth expected for 5G handsets. This represents a significant reversal in revenue driver trends and operational environment, directly impacting business performance expectations.
materiality.key_change: Reversal of handset demand volume outlook from decrease to increase

Such expected decline in demand is primarily driven by weakness in the macroeconomic environment (which has negatively impacted consumer demand for smartphones).
For calendar year 2024, we estimate that consumer demand for 3G, 4G, and 5G handset volumes will increase by a low-to-mid-single digit percentage relative to calendar year 2023.
This estimate includes expected high single-digit to low double-digit percentage growth in 5G handsets.

This reversal of trend and significant variance magnitude meaningfully changes the assessment of business recovery and demand drivers.
materiality.key_change: Reversal of QCT revenue trends with specific $2.8B shipment increase

sources.text: The decrease in QCT revenues in fiscal 2023 was primarily due to:

- lower handset revenues, primarily driven by $7.9 billion in lower chipset shipments to certain major OEMs (primarily driven by the negative effects of the macroeconomic environment weakness and customers drawing down on their elevated inventory levels), partially offset by $1.7 billion in higher revenues per chipset primarily driven by favorable mix and increases in average selling prices

- lower IoT revenues, primarily driven by a decrease in demand across consumer, edge networking, and industrial products (primarily driven by the negative effects of the macroeconomic environment weakness and elevated customer inventory levels)
+ higher automotive revenues, primarily driven by an increase in demand for digital cockpit products
The increase in QCT revenues in fiscal 2024 was primarily due to:

+ higher handsets revenues, due to $2.8 billion in higher chipset shipments driven by certain major OEMs (primarily driven by the normalization of customer inventory levels, which were elevated in the prior year), partially offset by $533 million in lower revenues per chipset primarily driven by unfavorable mix

sources.text: Others have proposed that injunctions should not be an available remedy for infringement of standard-essential patents and have made proposals that could severely limit damage awards and other remedies by courts for patent infringement (e.g., by limiting the base upon which the royalty rate may be applied).

In addition, governments may enact policies concerning standard-essential patents, such as the European Commission's proposed regulations which would create a new regulatory scheme for standard-essential patents, that may have various consequences, some of which may be detrimental, such as by devaluing standard-essential patents or disrupting worldwide technology standards.

We expect that such proposals, interpretations and strategies will continue in the future, and if successful, our business model would be harmed, either by limiting or eliminating our ability to collect royalties (or by reducing the royalties we can collect) on all or a portion of our standard-essential patent portfolio, limiting our return on investment with respect to new technologies, limiting our ability to seek injunctions against infringers of our standard-essential patents, constraining our ability to make licensing commitments when submitting our technologies for inclusion in future standards (which could make our technologies less likely to be included in such standards) or forcing us to work outside of SDOs or other industry groups to promote our new technologies, and our revenues, results of operations and cash flows could be negatively impacted.
We expect that such challenges, regardless of their merits, will continue into the foreseeable future and will require the investment of substantial management time and financial resources.

These strategies have included: (i) litigation, often alleging infringement of patents held by such companies, patent misuse, patent exhaustion, patent invalidity or unenforceability of our patents or licenses, alleging that we do not license our patents on fair, reasonable and nondiscriminatory (FRAND) terms, or alleging some form of unfair competition or competition law violation; (ii) taking positions contrary to our understanding (and/or the plain language) of their contracts with us; (iii) appeals to governmental authorities; (iv) collective action, including working with wireless operators, standards bodies, other like-minded companies and organizations, on both formal and informal bases, to adopt intellectual property policies and practices that could have the effect of limiting returns on intellectual property innovations; (v) lobbying governmental regulators and elected officials for the purpose of seeking the reduction of royalty rates or the base on which royalties are calculated, seeking to impose some form of compulsory licensing or weakening a patent holder's ability to enforce its rights or obtain a fair return for such rights; and (vi) attempts by licensees to shift their royalty obligation to their suppliers in order to make royalty collection more difficult or reduce the amount of royalties collected.

Some SDOs, courts and governmental agencies have adopted, and may in the future adopt, some or all of these interpretations or proposals in a manner adverse to our interests, including in litigation to which we may not be a party.

We expect that such proposals, interpretations and strategies will continue in the future, and if successful, our business model would be harmed, either by limiting or eliminating our ability to collect royalties (or by reducing the royalties we can collect) on all or a portion of our standard-essential patent portfolio, limiting our return on investment with respect to new technologies, limiting our ability to seek injunctions against infringers of our standard-essential patents, constraining our ability to make licensing commitments when submitting our technologies for inclusion in future standards (which could make our technologies less likely to be included in such standards) or forcing us to work outside of SDOs or other industry groups to promote our new technologies, and our business, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition could be negatively impacted.
